name: WV-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+22 partisan lean makes it one of the most Republican seats in the country
Incumbent Carol Miller holds a roughly 7-to-1 fundraising advantage over Vince George
Prediction markets price Miller's win probability near 98 percent
No public polling and no outside spending on the Democratic side
model.rationale: Miller pairs a safe incumbency and a dominant fundraising edge with an R+22 district, while the Democratic challenger has raised little and attracted no outside support; markets and fundamentals agree this is a safe Republican hold.
model.watch: Only a major scandal or a historic Democratic wave could put this seat in play, and neither sign is currently visible.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
West Virginia's first district is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, and incumbent Carol Miller is seeking reelection with the advantages that typically come with it. She has raised roughly $1.7 million and holds a large cash advantage over Democrat Vince George, who has about $258,000 on hand and has drawn little outside support. No public general-election polls are available, and no major expert raters have listed the race as competitive.

Prediction markets give Miller roughly a 98 percent chance of winning, in line with the district's R+22 partisan lean and the absence of any visible Democratic investment. A third-party candidate is on the ballot but is not a factor. Barring an extraordinary development, the seat is expected to remain in Republican hands by a wide margin in November.
